metrics.name: follow_up_questions
metrics.title: Follow-up questions
metrics.evidence: Most questions after the first implementation point at specific code or decisions, including vault_dir_exists, store_git vs pass(s) git, commit_meta_change, ensure_line, the vault_pass/vault_history split, 'what supplies vault_dir', 'is it right to hardcode vault here' and 'is this error message right'. Only someone who had read the output could ask those.

metrics.name: coding_guidelines
metrics.title: Coding guidelines
metrics.evidence: The git rules were in context and the commit subjects follow the type, lowercase and length rules, but five of seven use a `vault` scope in a non-monorepo where the rules say to omit it, so compliance is partial.

metrics.name: output_amendments
metrics.title: Output amendments
metrics.evidence: 948 of 847 generated lines were rewritten after the author challenged them

metrics.name: prompt_granularity
metrics.title: Prompt granularity
metrics.evidence: The median is 55 generated lines per producing prompt (13 of 43 prompts produced output), which falls in the 50 to 200 band; most prompts were small scoped requests, but 'Ok, implement this' (233 lines), 'Yes, keep a CHANGELOG...' (215) and 'Both' (212) exceeded the 200-line reviewable limit.

metrics.name: secondary_tools
metrics.title: Secondary tool usage
metrics.evidence: static checks not configured and did not run

metrics.name: generative_comments
metrics.title: Generative comments
metrics.evidence: 4 comment lines over 747 lines of code, against a repository baseline of 0.007
